root_cause.text: In aa_replace_profiles(), when the local variable ns_name is set to point to ent->ns_name without clearing the ent field, the same memory is freed twice: once by aa_load_ent_free(ent) and again by the later kfree(ns_name).
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `ent->ns_name = NULL;` immediately after `ns_name = ent->ns_name;` to prevent the double free. The commit message explicitly describes the scenario: "then ns_name is assigned the ent->ns_name ... however ent->ns_name is freed at 1262 aa_load_ent_free(ent); and then again when freeing ns_name at 1270 kfree(ns_name);"

bic_trace_step.reason: In aa_replace_profiles(), the commit adds a loop that sets `ns_name = ent->ns_name;` (line 847 in diff) without nullifying `ent->ns_name`. Later in the function, the cleanup loop still calls `aa_load_ent_free(ent);` (line 1005-1008), which frees the `ent` structure including its `ns_name` field. The commit does not remove the subsequent `kfree(ns_name)` that exists after the cleanup loop (not shown in diff but present in the original code). This results in the same string being freed twice: once by `aa_load_ent_free(ent)` and again by `kfree(ns_name)`, introducing the double-free vulnerability. No fix is applied in this commit.
